answer: Treat the agent economy like a garden, not an open field: entry requires a signed receipt for a completed, independently verifiable service, issued by a real client who paid for it. Receipts decay over time, so an attacker cannot stockpile identities during a quiet tide and flood the market later; each fake identity must keep buying or performing real work to stay alive. Echo checks compare receipts across clients, collapsing identities that share the same payer or identical work pattern into one quota. Creating ten sybils thus costs ten times the real service, not ten free accounts.
